steps.name: TF activity with decoupler ulm on CollecTRI

steps.description: This step answers the research question. constraints: Python only — decoupler mlm, not R
top_responsive_genes = 500 for PROGENy (R-0115)
Interpret footprint scores as footprints, not membership (R-0115)
SPIA-style topology-aware pathway impact is not available in this environment; do not claim topology was used (R-0122)

steps.description: Two complementary checks that make the T2S1 ranking interpretable rather than a bare list. steps.question: Which transcription factors are the defensible candidate drivers of the aldosterone response in these kidney samples, and how strong is the evidence for each?

grounding.reason: Activity report must state network, version, statistic, contrast, estimator, regulon size, regulator count and the inference caution (R-0119), with a full reproducibility record (R-0086).

Do not present the DE gene list as the answer — the question is about transcription factors
Do not upgrade any TF from hypothesis to established driver on the strength of this dataset alone
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T2S1 and T2S2. plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: TF activity inference
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks which transcription factors drive the aldosterone-treated kidney samples relative to vehicle controls. The input is a single gene-symbol-keyed raw Salmon count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv) with a 12-row metadata table carrying one condition column (6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle control, unpaired, single batch, Homo sapiens). Every script is Python, per the user constraint, so PyDESeq2 replaces the R DESeq2 path and the Python `decoupler` package replaces decoupleR.

The logic is: (T1S1) confirm sample structure before any inference — library sizes, VST-blind PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap coloured by condition; with n=6 per group a single mislabelled or degraded sample would dominate a TF activity score, so this must be checked first. (T1S2) fit the gene-level negative binomial model with PyDESeq2 (Wald test, aldosterone as numerator, control as denominator, explicitly set), minimally pre-filtered at >=10 counts in >=6 samples, BH at alpha 0.05, with ashr shrinkage for reported effect sizes; the Wald statistic of every tested gene — not the significant subset — is the ranking input the TF step needs. (T2S1) infer TF activity two ways with decoupler ulm on the CollecTRI human signed regulons: contrast-level activity from the full Wald-statistic vector, and per-sample activity from the log2 CPM matrix, then test the per-sample scores between the two conditions with a moderated/ordinary t-test and BH across regulators. The two views must agree for a TF to be reported as a driver. (T2S2) adds PROGENy pathway-footprint activity (mlm) as upstream context for the TF calls, and a target-level sanity check: for each top TF, the direction and effect size of its own transcript and of its leading-edge targets. (T1S3) assembles the report with the reproducibility record and the explicit caution that an activity score is an inference from a prior literature network, not a measurement.

Key constraints on interpretation: 12 samples is adequate for a two-group DE test but the TF scores are derived quantities whose uncertainty is not fully propagated; CollecTRI is tissue-agnostic, so a kidney-specific regulator with few curated edges can be missed and a regulon whose targets are silent in kidney adds noise. A network inferred from this expression matrix itself (ARACNe/VIPER style) is not possible at n=12 and is not planned. The known aldosterone/mineralocorticoid-receptor axis (NR3C2, and the SGK1/SCNN1 downstream programme) is a positive control the report should state explicitly — its presence or absence in the ranking is informative either way and must not be used to select the ranking.

steps.method: VST(blind) PCA, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples
decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI regulons, on the Wald statistic and on the per-sample log2 CPM matrix
decoupleR mlm on PROGENy footprint model
Activity report with network version, statistic, estimator, regulon size, reproducibility record

Output states in writing that an activity score is an inference from a prior network, not a measurement, and that a high score is a hypothesis for follow-up
Whether NR3C2 / the mineralocorticoid axis appears is reported explicitly, as an observation rather than a selection criterion
constraints: Python only — the `decoupler` Python package, not R decoupleR. rpy2 permitted solely to deserialize an .rda network if the DoRothEA fallback is used
Use ulm as the estimator; mlm may be reported as a robustness check only (R-0111)
Run ulm on the FULL ranked statistic vector of every tested gene, never on the significant subset only (R-0111)
Keep the sign of each edge — mode of regulation must not be discarded (R-0113 / CollecTRI weights)
min_regulon_size = 5 targets among the tested genes (R-0111)
Test per-sample scores between groups and adjust with BH across regulators (R-0112)
Do NOT infer a regulatory network from this expression matrix — 12 samples cannot support mutual-information network inference; a prior knowledge network is the only sound source here (R-0121)
Match the organism: use the HUMAN network, never the mouse or rat file
caveats: VIPER on an ARACNe tissue-specific regulon is the tool of record for context-specific regulator activity and is absent from this environment; decoupler on a prior network is the substitute. A prior network is tissue-agnostic, so a kidney-specific regulator can be missed and a target silent in kidney adds noise (R-0114)
TF activity scores are derived from a gene-level model; their uncertainty is not fully propagated into the between-group test, so the per-TF p-values are optimistic
With 12 samples the per-sample score comparison has 10 residual degrees of freedom — report effect sizes alongside p-values and do not over-read a marginal BH-adjusted value
A TF's own transcript need not change for its activity to change; do not require concordance between TF expression and TF activity, but do report both

grounding.reason: TF activity is the research question: decoupler ulm on signed CollecTRI human regulons, run both on the contrast Wald statistic (R-0111) and per-sample on the log matrix with a between-group test and BH across regulators (R-0112); prior network only at n=12 (R-0121).

steps.name: Pathway footprint context and TF target-level check
steps.question: Which upstream signalling footprints accompany the TF activity changes in aldosterone-treated kidney, and do the individual targets of the top-ranked TFs move in the direction their regulon sign predicts?
steps.description: Two complementary checks that make the T2S1 ranking interpretable rather than a bare list. (a) Pathway footprint: run decoupler's multivariate linear model (mlm) with the PROGENy human footprint model on the Wald statistic vector from T1S2, using the top 500 responsive genes per pathway, and report one activity score and BH-adjusted p-value per pathway. If the PROGENy model is not resolvable from the reference store or from the decoupler data loaders offline, report that explicitly and skip part (a) without failing the step — it is context, not the answer. (b) Target-level audit: for each of the top ~10 TFs from T2S1, tabulate its own expression change (log2FC, padj from T1S2) and the distribution of Wald statistics of its regulon targets split by activating vs repressing edges, so a reader can see whether the score rests on many coherent small target changes or on a handful of extreme genes. Report the number of targets present and the leading-edge targets driving each score. Read the pathway scores as transcriptional footprints, not as expression of the pathway members.
steps.context: Aldosterone acts through the mineralocorticoid receptor; a footprint model may surface the accompanying signalling context (e.g. MAPK, NFkB, p53 axes) around the TF calls. This step is supporting evidence for the T2S1 answer, not a second answer.
acceptance_criteria: PROGENy mlm pathway activity table with score, p-value and BH-adjusted p-value per pathway, top 500 responsive genes per pathway stated — or an explicit written statement that the footprint model could not be resolved and why
Per-TF target audit for the top TFs from T2S1: target count, activating/repressing split, distribution of target Wald statistics, and the leading-edge targets
Each top TF's own log2FC and padj reported beside its activity score
Written statement that a pathway footprint score is not the expression of the pathway's member genes
constraints: Python only — decoupler mlm, not R
top_responsive_genes = 500 for PROGENy (R-0115)
Interpret footprint scores as footprints, not membership (R-0115)
SPIA-style topology-aware pathway impact is not available in this environment; do not claim topology was used (R-0122)
If the PROGENy resource is absent, degrade gracefully: report the absence and deliver part (b) alone
caveats: The PROGENy footprint model is trained largely on cell-line perturbation data; its transfer to human kidney tissue is an assumption, not a validated mapping
A TF score driven by two or three extreme targets is fragile — the target audit exists specifically to expose that case

grounding.reason: Pathway activity as context for the TF calls: decoupler mlm on the PROGENy footprint model with 500 responsive genes per pathway (R-0115); topology-aware SPIA is absent so no topology claim is made (R-0122).

steps.name: Integrated report and reproducibility record
steps.question: Which transcription factors are the defensible candidate drivers of the aldosterone response in these kidney samples, and how strong is the evidence for each?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T2S1 and T2S2. Lead with the answer: the ranked candidate TF drivers for aldosterone vs vehicle control, each with its contrast-level ulm score and BH-adjusted p-value, its per-sample between-group test result, its regulon size, the direction of activity change, and whether the two views agreed. State for every activity result: the network name and version, the input statistic, the contrast (aldosterone vs control), the estimator (ulm), the minimum regulon size, and the number of regulators tested. State plainly that an activity score is an inference from a curated prior network and not a measurement, so each top TF is a hypothesis for experimental follow-up. Include the QC verdict and any flagged sample, the DE summary counts, the p-value histogram diagnostic, and the pathway footprint context. Report the power limitation honestly: 6 vs 6 samples, activity scores derived from a gene-level fit whose uncertainty is not propagated, and a tissue-agnostic regulon. Close with a reproducibility record: package versions for pydeseq2/decoupler/pandas/numpy/scipy/statsmodels, any random seeds used, the regulon collection name and version, and the session info.
steps.context: Final synthesis for a single-question analysis: the deliverable is the TF driver list with calibrated confidence, not a gene list.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked TF driver table presented first, with score, BH-adjusted p-value, regulon size, direction, and cross-view agreement per TF
Network name, version, input statistic, contrast, estimator, min regulon size, and number of regulators tested all stated (R-0119)
Explicit inference caution that an activity score is not a measurement
QC verdict, flagged samples, DE summary counts, and p-value histogram shape all carried into the report
Sample-size and prior-network limitations stated in plain language, not buried
Reproducibility record with package versions, seeds, and regulon collection version (R-0086)
constraints: Python only
Do not present the DE gene list as the answer — the question is about transcription factors
Do not upgrade any TF from hypothesis to established driver on the strength of this dataset alone
caveats: Agreement with prior literature on the aldosterone/mineralocorticoid axis is reassuring but is not independent validation, since the regulon network is itself literature-derived — say so

grounding.reason: Activity report must state network, version, statistic, contrast, estimator, regulon size, regulator count and the inference caution (R-0119), with a full reproducibility record (R-0086).
